topic: DevSpace Ultra: Multi-Agent Workspace with ChatGPT Classic Workers

key_points: MIT-licensed distribution of DevSpace with an elastic ChatGPT Classic multi-agent runtime layer
Keeps upstream DevSpace local MCP workspace (files, code search, editing, terminal, artifacts, skills, self-hosting)
Adds production-oriented Chat Swarm control plane for running multiple independent ChatGPT Classic worker conversations on one computer
Elastic worker pool: main agent scales workers up/down by workload; live Swarm resize without losing completed work
Independent ChatGPT Classic runtimes on Windows (isolated package identities, profiles, sessions, conversations)
Same-worker context continuity: reopen worker at exact saved ChatGPT conversation and continue with held worker token
Zero-copy bootstrap: launch, minimize, send into sub-agents ChatGPT Project, join Swarm, park without manual invite-code copy/paste
Backend-first routing: normal work dispatched through Chat Swarm backend; UI/CDP automation is lifecycle/bootstrap/recovery only
Recovery: detects missing runtimes, interrupted connections, stale worker loops, blocking UI notices; reopens exact worker conversation
Update compatibility manager: canary runtime, profile backup, rolling worker update, exact-conversation restore, verification, rollback
Configurable runtime reservation (reservedWorkers); no runtime reserved by default

v0.2.0 adds local-first DevSpace Browser Control (Chrome extension, exclusive per-tab claims, AGENT CLAIMED THIS TAB strip, semantic accessibility snapshots, screenshots + console/network diagnostics)

v0.3 adds Unified Agent Capability Runtime: capability_* surface for discovering/installing/inspecting/enabling/updating/isolating/calling reusable capabilities; understands Agent Skills, instruction packs, MCP tools/prompts/resources, DevSpace manifests, Claude/Codex plugin metadata, MCP Registry metadata
One-click install: Windows PowerShell irm ...install.ps1 | iex; macOS/Linux curl -fsSL ...install.sh | bash; npm install -g github:enwong93-sketch/devspace-ultra#main

Requirements: Node >=22.19 <27 (22 LTS recommended), Windows 10/11 x64 for automatic isolated desktop runtime cloning, ChatGPT Classic Windows Desktop app signed in, 16GB RAM for 2-4 workers / 32GB+ for larger pools, no GPU required

Platform support: base MCP workspace + Chat Swarm backend + manual/browser workers + elastic resize on Win/macOS/Linux; automatic isolated desktop runtime cloning + recovery + canary/rolling update manager are Windows-only
Production flow: assess workload -> choose desiredWorkers -> elastic scale runtime + Swarm capacity -> dispatch -> collect/synthesize -> shrink idle tail workers
Runtime tools: chat_swarm_runtime_status/ensure/scale/recover/autojoin/setup/stop, chat_swarm_elastic_scale, chat_swarm_update_status/rollout

Chat Swarm backend: create/join/status, dispatch/collect/cancel, long parked worker waits and submit/repark, targeted or first-available routing, idempotent taskKey retries, persistence across restart, worker recycle fallback, safe live capacity resize
Elastic scaling separates runtime capacity from task routing; scaling down only removes safe idle tail capacity, never interrupts busy worker
sub-agents Project routing: new worker conversations created inside configured ChatGPT Project instead of cluttering general chat list

Security: self-hosted MCP model, keep server bound/exposed only through controlled transport, use auth; worker/orchestrator tokens not written to normal controller logs; Browser Control uses one-time pairing + exclusive per-tab claims, persists only hashes of tokens
GitHub stats: 35 stars, 5 forks, created 2026-08-18, JavaScript, MIT

DevSpace is a small self-hosted MCP server that lets ChatGPT open a real project folder, read/edit files, run shell commands, show diffs — same loop as Codex/Claude Code but on your laptop with your existing ChatGPT subscription
Plain ChatGPT chat has no filesystem access; Code Interpreter only runs Python in throwaway container; Codex works against cloned repo in cloud sandbox, not the folder open in your editor
On July 9, 2026 OpenAI merged standalone Codex app into single ChatGPT desktop app (Chat, Work, Codex modes, every plan incl Free) and shipped GPT-5.6 model family
DevSpace is free/open-source (MIT, npm package v1.0.4); catch: custom Plugins live behind ChatGPT Developer Mode which requires Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu — not Free plan

Setup: npm install -g @waishnav/devspace, devspace init to pick allowed folders + port (default 7676), tunnel port publicly (e.g. ssh -p 443 -R0:localhost:7676 free.pinggy.io), devspace serve, devspace doctor
In ChatGPT web: Settings -> Security and login -> enable Developer mode -> add Plugin pointing at https://your-tunnel/mcp; approve with Owner password from ~/.devspace/auth.json
Requirements: Node >=22.19 <27, npm, Git, Bash-compatible shell (Git Bash or WSL on Windows), public HTTPS tunnel; Linux/macOS/Windows supported, plain PowerShell/cmd.exe not yet

Default minimal tool mode exposes 4 tools + entry point: open_workspace, read, write, edit, bash; full tool mode adds grep/glob/ls; experimental codex mode swaps in apply_patch/exec_command/write_stdin mirroring Codex CLI
First commit June 14, 2026 — genuinely new project, not everything polished yet
